exposure: Gluten immunogenic peptides (GIP) in amniotic fluid
outcome: Detectability of GIP in amniotic fluid
Correlation between foetal GIP exposure and maternal gluten intake
cohort: The study included 125 pregnant women with varying gluten diets and gestational ages.
finding: The study found that gluten immunogenic peptides (GIP) are detectable in amniotic fluid from at least the 16th gestational week in gluten-consuming women and established a positive correlation between foetal GIP exposure and maternal gluten intake, suggesting a novel closed-loop circuit involving foetal swallowing and excretion of GIP.
cross-section timing: During pregnancy, from at least the 16th gestational week onwards, and into late pregnancy.
gest_age: From at least the 16th gestational week onwards
